title: Here’s the secret to creating flexible, automated T&E policies
summary: Discover how Navan’s custom user attributes bridge the gap between your HR data and ERP controls to scale compliance without manual intervention.
body_markdown:
Let’s face it: Companies aren’t carbon copies — they’re snowflakes, and each comes with its own unique culture and structure. Also unique is how they think about their teams, business units, and ERPs — as well as how policy should map individuals to those aspects of the organization.


To handle the nuances, some expense management systems have forced customers to make a painful choice: Choke your employees with restrictive guardrails, or make your finance team scramble to make sense of a structure that isn’t properly reflected in an organization’s policies and reporting.


It’s not a choice companies should have to make.


That’s why we’ve introduced custom user attributes. Navan admins can now create and manage up to 10 custom fields — such as Business Unit, Employment Type, Project Area, or Level — and map them automatically via HRIS integrations, Okta SCIM, or SFTP. Crucially, these attributes can be targeted directly within your travel and expense policies and reporting to ensure your spend rules automatically align with the unique structure of your global workforce.


Here’s why this functionality is essential — and how your organization can put it to use.


## The core challenge: The gap between HR data and T&E control


As organizations scale, corporate directory data and ERP schemas become highly complex. Legacy expense systems require administrative teams to build manual workarounds to accommodate this complexity, while newer fintech platforms often rely on flat, rigid user structures that can’t “speak the language” of your HRIS or ERP.


The result? Manual data entry errors, policy gaps, and hours of post-trip accounting cleanup to map transactions to the right ledger accounts.


Navan’s custom user attributes bridge this gap by acting as the essential, flexible plumbing that connects your source-of-truth employee data to your spend controls. Your company gets enterprise-grade compliance and reporting precision without sacrificing operational simplicity.


## Two ways to optimize your policy logic


With Navan’s custom user attributes, admins can move beyond basic parameters, like department or office location, to build policy logic across two primary dimensions:


### 1. User-dependent policies


Apply rules dynamically based on who the employee is: their team, product area, tenure, contract type, or seniority level. Instead of manually selecting specific individuals for a policy, you can build permanent policy rules that target custom user traits. When employee details are updated in your HRIS, their travel limits and spending policies are updated in Navan — instantly and automatically.


### 2. Trip-dependent policies


Control spending based on the specific purpose of the travel, such as the associated client, project code, or event. This allows organizations to establish tighter control on project-based travel, while helping to ensure that project costs are accurately tracked and billed.


This feature has been an enormous benefit for SpotOn, a fast, flexible point-of-sale for full-service restaurants and bars. “We added a customer ID attribute for our teams that are traveling for customer implementations and other customer-related expenses,” said Jack Chalfant, SpotOn’s controller. “That helps us to track expenses more closely at a customer level.”


## Automation in action


Here’s how forward-thinking finance teams are using custom attributes to eliminate manual intervention and clean up their accounting pipelines:


### Scenario 1: Mapping expenses to NetSuite business units


- **The problem:** A company needs to map travel expenses to distinct “Business Units” within NetSuite. However, their standard user directory only supports basic department fields, forcing the accounting team to manually re-classify thousands of dollars in travel spend during month-end close.
- **The solution:** The admin creates a custom user attribute in Navan named “Business Unit,” which maps directly to NetSuite. Because the correct business unit data is captured automatically at the user level, transactions flow cleanly into the ERP with nearly eliminating any manual cleanup.


### Scenario 2: Dynamic spending limits for contractors vs. full-time employees


- **The problem:** A business enforces lower daily travel stipends for contract workers than for full-time employees. Without a way to differentiate them automatically, admins have to manually assign new contractors to specific policy groups every time they’re onboarded — a process prone to human error and policy leaks.
- **The solution:** The admin adds an “Employment Type” custom user field, then builds a policy rule that automatically applies the correct contractor spending limits to anyone carrying that attribute. As new contractors sync to Navan via Okta or SFTP, the correct travel limits are applied — instantly and automatically.


### Scenario 3: Splitting policies by ERP system


- **The problem:** A large enterprise manages global operations across eight different ERPs. Standard directory fields don’t account for this complexity, making it impossible to enforce policies based on an employee’s connected financial system.
- **The solution:** The admin creates a custom attribute called “ERP.” Every user is assigned their specific ERP, and the finance team builds policies that dynamically trigger based on that assignment. It’s a creative way to use the feature to solve a complex, non-traditional infrastructure challenge.


## Why this matters: Custom-designed spend programs based on company structure


By leveraging custom user attributes, finance leaders gain:


- **More flexibility:** Build policies that genuinely reflect the operational reality of your business — not the limitations of your software.
- **Granular control:** Target specific spend guidelines, down to individual project teams, contract types, or management tiers.
- **Automation at scale:** Eliminate the administrative overhead of managing exceptions. Let your HR directory sync handle policy provisioning cleanly and automatically.
- **Pain-free month-end closes:** By ensuring that transactions are tagged with the right custom attributes at the point of spend, your ERP data remains pristine, saving hours of manual reconciliation. “Having Navan reflect our accounting and ERP department structure simplifies our reporting,” said SpotOn’s Chalfant.


Enterprise-grade control and compliance, designed with consumer-grade simplicity: At Navan, that’s what we do — and the custom user attributes functionality is one more way we’re making life easier for our many thousands of customers.
